stories.title: Thrones of Delhi and Agra
stories.blurb: How the Mughals won, lost, rebuilt and fought over the twin capitals of the Yamuna, from Babur's guns at Panipat to the succession battle at Jajau.

steps.name: First Battle of Panipat
steps.what: Babur's small army with matchlocks and field guns destroyed the Lodi host.
steps.why: It ended the Delhi Sultanate and opened north India to Mughal rule.

steps.name: Battle of Khanwa
steps.what: Babur defeated the Rajput confederacy near Sikri.
steps.why: It secured Agra and the Mughal hold on the Ganga plain.

steps.date_note: Humayun was beaten at Kannauj, east of this map
steps.name: Sher Shah takes the capitals
steps.what: The Afghan Sher Shah drove Humayun into exile and ruled from Delhi and Agra.
steps.why: His roads, revenue and coins outlasted his dynasty.

steps.name: Humayun dies at the library stairs
steps.what: Months after retaking Delhi, Humayun fell on the steps of the Sher Mandal.
steps.why: A thirteen-year-old Akbar inherited a fragile kingdom.

steps.name: Second Battle of Panipat
steps.what: Hemu, who had taken Delhi in October, was wounded by an arrow and lost.
steps.why: The victory made Mughal rule in Hindustan permanent.

steps.name: Agra Fort in red sandstone
steps.what: Akbar rebuilt the fort at Agra as the seat of a centralised state.
steps.why: It announced Agra as the imperial capital.

steps.name: A capital at Sikri
steps.what: Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri beside the saint who had foretold his sons.
steps.why: For fourteen years the court, debates and studios lived here.

steps.name: Akbar dies at Agra
steps.what: Akbar died in the fort and Salim took the throne as Jahangir.
steps.why: The transition held despite Prince Khusrau's challenge.

steps.name: Nur Jahan
steps.what: Jahangir married the widow Mehr-un-Nissa.
steps.why: Her family dominated the court for two decades.

steps.name: The court moves to Shahjahanabad
steps.what: Shah Jahan entered his new palace fortress at Delhi.
steps.why: Delhi again became the centre of Mughal power.

steps.name: Battle of Samugarh
steps.what: Aurangzeb broke the heir apparent's army east of Agra.
steps.why: Within weeks Shah Jahan was a prisoner in Agra Fort.

steps.name: Dara Shikoh executed
steps.what: After being paraded through Delhi, Dara was put to death.
steps.why: It closed the war of succession and silenced Dara's eclectic party.

steps.name: Jat rising at Tilpat
steps.what: Jat peasants rose against Mughal officials south of Delhi.
steps.why: It began a long Jat revolt around Agra and Mathura.

steps.name: Battle of Jajau
steps.what: After Aurangzeb's death in the Deccan his sons fought near Agra.
steps.why: The empire passed on, but the age of the great Mughals was over.

stories.title: Markets, Workshops and Ideas
stories.blurb: Coins, roads, indigo and marble: how money, craft and argument moved through the Mughal capitals, told through merchants, painters, translators and travellers.

steps.name: The silver rupiya
steps.what: Sher Shah struck a silver coin of standard weight.
steps.why: It became the basis of Mughal and later Indian money.

steps.name: Sarais on the great road
steps.what: Rest houses and wells lined the road through Delhi and Agra.
steps.why: Merchants, couriers and pilgrims moved faster and safer.

steps.name: The Hamzanama studio
steps.what: Persian and Indian painters worked together on a giant illustrated romance.
steps.why: It created the Mughal painting style.

steps.name: The Ibadat Khana debates
steps.what: Scholars of many faiths argued before Akbar.
steps.why: Their arguments shaped the policy of universal tolerance.

steps.name: Measuring the harvest
steps.what: Cash revenue was fixed from ten-year averages of crops and prices.
steps.why: Peasant taxes paid for the army and the cities.

steps.name: Ralph Fitch counts the crowds
steps.what: An English merchant found Agra and Fatehpur Sikri each bigger than London.
steps.why: It shows how large the Mughal capitals were.

steps.name: Ain-i-Akbari
steps.what: Abul Fazl recorded prices, wages, crafts and revenue.
steps.why: It is the main source for the Mughal economy.

steps.name: Indigo at Bayana
steps.what: Dutch and English buyers bid for Bayana indigo.
steps.why: Agra's hinterland was tied into world trade.

steps.name: Pelsaert on wages
steps.what: A Dutch factor contrasted court luxury with workers' poverty.
steps.why: It is a rare look at ordinary life in Agra.

steps.name: Marble and inlay for the Taj
steps.what: Thousands of masons and inlayers built the Taj.
steps.why: It made Agra the centre of pietra dura craft.

steps.name: A merchant's half-story
steps.what: A Jain trader wrote his life in verse at Agra.
steps.why: It shows debts, partnerships and fears of a merchant under the Mughals.

steps.name: Chandni Chowk opens
steps.what: Jahanara laid out a market street and caravanserai in Delhi.
steps.why: It became the commercial heart of Shahjahanabad.

steps.name: Upanishads in Persian
steps.what: Dara had fifty Upanishads translated at Delhi.
steps.why: Through a later Latin version they reached European philosophy.

steps.name: Jizya returns
steps.what: Aurangzeb reimposed the poll tax that Akbar had abolished.
steps.why: It reversed a century of policy and stirred protest.
